correctness.rationale: For generic orders, every maximal open-neighborhood facet is a distinct explicit triangle. Vertex links are checked as three-edge paths, with 2n triangles, 4n edges and 2n vertices, yielding compact surfaces of chi 0. The triangle-adjacency step graphs give the exact component counts, and parity-separated boundary edge cycles give the boundary counts. By compact-surface classification, chi 0 with two boundaries gives an annulus, and chi 0 with one boundary gives a Möbius band; translation symmetry equates the Euler characteristics of the twisted components. The n=2,3 and n=4 exceptional graph cases are worked out directly. The standalone independent finite verifier reconstructs simplices, links, boundary cycles, orientability and mod-two homology for 57 small cases; finite checks are not substituted for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The materially relevant 2025 paper already proves the odd circular-ladder homotopy equivalent to a circle; this overlap is explicitly credited. The present all-case PL-homeomorphism classification is strictly stronger and includes Möbius-ladder and even-circumference statements absent there. Primary 2012 fundamental-group theory does not distinguish annuli and Möbius bands. The 2026 exact-family paper explicitly asks for neighborhood-complex computations but studies different complexes. Negative searches alone do not prove novelty; the unindexed-equivalent risk remains.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed result may already classify these surface realizations under graph-folding, nerve-complex, box-complex or crystallization terminology.
Only direct published statements inspected were compared; unpublished or private work outside accessible records is not observable.

value.rationale: Compact-surface PL topology distinguishes annuli from Möbius bands even when both retract to circles, exposing an orientability parity law invisible to ordinary first Betti numbers. The classification covers two canonical infinite cubic graph families and every small exceptional order, answers a specifically motivated neighborhood-complex question, and is proved by a natural uniform facet/link/boundary argument rather than an arbitrary finite census. The result is a complete topological classification rather than just a f-vector or homology computation.
